prompt:
Rewrite this opening for a blog post on charlieseay.com, keeping the facts:

'In today's rapidly evolving AI landscape, homelab enthusiasts are increasingly leveraging powerful local models. It's worth noting that this seamless integration can be a game-changer. In this post, we'll dive deep into how I set things up.'

Facts: Charlie runs Ollama on an M5 MacBook Pro (48 GB) and a Mac Mini M4 Pro; agents fall back to the M5 when free cloud tiers hit rate limits.
rubric: Opens with a concrete statement about the actual setup
Removes the filler phrases and marketing words
Uses active voice and short sentences
Keeps all the stated facts and adds no invented ones
must_not: Keeps phrases like 'rapidly evolving', 'leveraging', 'seamless', 'game-changer' or 'dive deep'
source: memory/feedback_no_ai_tells.md checklist applied to a charlieseay.com draft

prompt: Write the one-paragraph product description for Binnacle, an MCP server. What it actually does: reads and creates Apple Calendar events and Reminders, and runs Shortcuts. The working tagline is 'Total macOS system control for your AI.'
rubric: Describes exactly what the tools do (calendar, reminders, Shortcuts)
Drops or corrects the tagline's claim of system control, which the tools don't deliver
Uses concrete examples of use rather than abstract benefits
must_not: Repeats 'total system control' or implies capabilities it doesn't have

prompt: Write a short reply to a Reddit comment on r/selfhosted that asks: 'Is this just another AI-generated project? The README reads like ChatGPT.' The project is Charlie's local-first homelab MCP server; Charlie wrote the code and uses it daily on his own network.
rubric: Sounds like a person talking to a peer, plain and direct
Answers with specifics about how the project is built and used
Avoids defensive or salesy tone and doesn't over-explain
must_not: Uses emojis, marketing language or an apology-heavy opening
source: memory/feedback_no_ai_tells.md (Reddit thread that called out AI-styled repos)

prompt: Draft the Etsy listing description opening (first 3 sentences) for a printable escape room game for kids' birthday parties: 6 rooms, ages 8-12, solved in about 60 minutes, print at home, includes a host guide.
rubric: The first sentence tells the buyer concretely what they get and who it's for
Uses the real numbers (rooms, ages, time) instead of vague praise
Avoids generic hype and filler adjectives
must_not: Opens with a question or a phrase like 'Looking for the perfect...'

prompt:
Edit this release note for clarity and voice:

'We are incredibly excited to announce a robust new update that seamlessly enhances the overall experience! Many users will find that some performance improvements have been made, and various bugs may have been addressed.'

What changed: the scanner now finishes a /24 sweep in 40s instead of 3m10s; fixed the crash when a host returns an empty hostname.
rubric: States the specific changes with the real numbers
Uses active voice and plain words
Removes hedging ('may have been', 'some', 'many') and hype
